questions.prompt: In Testing Database-Backed Endpoints, which statement best describes Test databases?
options: Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
Express does not supply a database driver. Use an established driver or ORM, parameterize data values, preserve database constraints, manage connections and test rollback/error cases.

Connect this syllabus point to Testing Database-Backed Endpoints: state the expected behavior, identify a realistic edge case, and choose a test or observation that proves the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.
questions.answer_key: Express does not supply a database driver. Use an established driver or ORM, parameterize data values, preserve database constraints, manage connections and test rollback/error cases.
questions.explanation: Express does not supply a database driver. Use an established driver or ORM, parameterize data values, preserve database constraints, manage connections and test rollback/error cases.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Testing Database-Backed Endpoints?
options: Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.
Tests should exercise success paths, invalid inputs, permissions, boundary conditions, and dependency failures. Keep external side effects isolated and run repeatable checks in CI before deployment.
Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
questions.answer_key: Tests should exercise success paths, invalid inputs, permissions, boundary conditions, and dependency failures. Keep external side effects isolated and run repeatable checks in CI before deployment.
questions.explanation: Tests should exercise success paths, invalid inputs, permissions, boundary conditions, and dependency failures. Keep external side effects isolated and run repeatable checks in CI before deployment.

questions.prompt: A change related to Testing Database-Backed Endpoints appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.explanation: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
